name: Clomiphene
summary: A prescription fertility pill that triggers ovulation in women who don't ovulate regularly; it is also used off-label in men to raise their own testosterone.
what_it_is: Clomiphene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) taken as a tablet. It raises the pituitary hormones LH and FSH, which in women leads to ovulation and in men stimulates the testes to make testosterone. It is a mix of two forms, enclomiphene and zuclomiphene (30% to 50% of the mix); zuclomiphene stays in the body for more than a month.

evidence.why: FDA-approved for ovulation induction; in men, a 2025 meta-analysis of 10 randomized trials (819 men) found it raises testosterone, with mixed effects on symptoms.

status_us.label: FDA-approved for ovulation induction; off-label in men
status_us.note: Approved to treat ovulatory dysfunction in women who want to become pregnant. The label says there are no adequate or well-controlled studies in male infertility, so use in men is off-label.

benefits.claim: Induces ovulation in women with ovulatory dysfunction; about 30% of treated patients became pregnant in the label's studies
Raises total testosterone, LH and FSH in men with low testosterone compared with placebo (10 randomized trials, 819 men; moderate-certainty evidence)
Clomiphene or enclomiphene preserved sperm counts better than testosterone gel at similar testosterone levels: men were much less likely to have a low sperm concentration (risk ratio 0.10)
Improved symptom scores (ADAM questionnaire) in mostly observational studies of men with hypogonadism; results in randomized trials were mixed
Lowered IGF-1 by about 41% on average, and to normal in 7 of 16, when added to treatment in men with acromegaly that standard therapy hadn't controlled (small open-label study; off-label)

risks.risk: Ovarian enlargement (13.6%), hot flashes (10.4%) and abdominal or pelvic discomfort or bloating (5.5%)
Visual symptoms such as blurring, spots or flashes (1.5%), more likely with higher total dose or longer use; the label says to stop treatment if they occur, and they can be long-lasting or permanent
Multiple pregnancy, in about 8% of pregnancies in trials
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, which can progress within a day to several days and become serious
Possible higher risk of borderline or invasive ovarian tumors with prolonged use
In men, side effects were reported in under 10% of study participants, including headache and drowsiness; the label notes reports of testicular tumors and breast enlargement in men

IGF-1 can fall: in a small study of 20 men treated for low testosterone it fell in 15, and in 2 it dropped well below normal; the authors suggest checking IGF-1 during treatment, and it isn't known whether the drop matters

avoid_if: Liver disease or a history of liver problems
Abnormal uterine bleeding of unknown cause
Ovarian cysts or enlargement not caused by polycystic ovary syndrome
Uncontrolled thyroid or adrenal problems, or a pituitary tumor or other brain lesion

before: Men: morning total testosterone, LH, FSH and estradiol
Semen analysis if fertility is a goal
during: Eye exam if vision changes occur
labs.why: For women, the label rules out pregnancy and ovarian cysts before treatment; for off-label use in men there is no label guidance, and trials tracked testosterone, LH, FSH, estradiol and hematocrit; a 2025 study found IGF-1 fell in most men treated for low testosterone, and its authors suggest checking it.

studies.title: Clomiphene or enclomiphene citrate for the treatment of male hypogonadism: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
studies.people: 819 men with hypogonadism in 10 randomized trials
studies.finding: Clomiphene or enclomiphene raised total testosterone, LH and FSH versus placebo; testosterone levels were similar to testosterone gel, but sperm counts were better preserved. Symptom results were mixed.

studies.title: Clomiphene citrate for men with hypogonadism: a systematic review and meta-analysis
studies.people: 1,642 men with hypogonadism in 19 studies (4 randomized)
studies.finding: Testosterone, LH, FSH and estradiol rose during treatment and symptom scores improved; side effects were reported in under 10% of participants and none were serious.

studies.title: Clomiphene Citrate Tablets, USP: Prescribing Information
studies.finding: About 30% of treated patients became pregnant; multiple pregnancies made up about 8% of pregnancies.

studies.title: Reduced IGF-1 Levels Following Clomiphene Treatment for Male Hypogonadism
studies.people: 20 men treated for low testosterone (median age 47), most with pituitary disease
studies.finding: IGF-1 fell in 15 of 20 men (a median of 0.6 standard deviations), and in 2 it dropped well below the normal range for age and sex, while testosterone rose in all of them. The authors call the clinical importance unknown and suggest checking IGF-1 during treatment.

studies.title: Clomiphene citrate added to treatment in men with acromegaly not controlled by standard therapy (Duarte, Jallad and Bronstein)
studies.people: 16 men with acromegaly and low testosterone whose disease wasn't controlled
studies.finding: Adding clomiphene for 3 months lowered IGF-1 by about 41% on average (424 to 250 ng/mL) and brought it to normal in 7 of 16; testosterone roughly doubled.

ask_your_clinician: For men: would clomiphene protect my fertility better than testosterone therapy?
Which vision changes mean I should stop and get checked?
How will we watch for ovarian enlargement or hyperstimulation?

notes_for_editor: Clomiphene is approved only for women. Studies in men are mostly small or observational; the 2025 meta-analysis rated certainty moderate for hormone levels and low for some comparisons, and its authors' suggestion that it is a viable alternative to testosterone gel goes beyond their symptom data. Hematocrit appears in the labs because the 2025 review noted discontinuations for raised hematocrit in some trial arms. The label used is a generic (Cosette) label from August 2025; the brand Clomid label was not checked. The label also says long-term cyclic use is not recommended beyond a limited number of cycles. Enclomiphene, one of its two isomers, has its own entry. Added 2026-11-06: the IGF-1 lowering, from the Mogar 2025 full text (Journal of the Endocrine Society, read on the publisher's site) and the Duarte 2015 abstract (PMID 25738590, read through a PubMed mirror; its exact title wasn't confirmed, so the source names it by its authors). Both used clomiphene, not enclomiphene alone.
